Scenario.CropWatch.Briefing: Map the world's farmland every 8 days for 5 years.
Scenario.CropWatch.Lesson: NASA flew one big, capable, long-lived satellite, and paired it with Landsat 8 to halve the revisit time.
Scenario.StormChaser.Briefing: Look inside tropical storms at least every 2 hours for 2 years.
Scenario.StormChaser.Lesson: NASA flew several tiny satellites, because many small ones revisit a storm far more often than one big one.

Tour.Title: Look around
Tour.Scale: Spacecraft are drawn far larger than life, or they would be invisible next to the Earth.
Landmark.Station.About: A laboratory the size of a football field, with a crew on board without a break since November 2000.
Landmark.Hubble.About: A telescope the size of a school bus that has watched the universe from above the atmosphere since 1990.
Landmark.Landsat.About: The latest in a line of satellites that have mapped the Earth's land since 1972. It is the real mission behind Crop Watch.
Landmark.Goes.About: It hangs over one spot on the equator, so it can watch the same storms around the clock.
Landmark.Webb.About: An infrared telescope parked 1.5 million km away, shaded from the Sun by a shield the size of a tennis court.
